Heterogeneous Volumetric Raymarching is a rendering technique for participating media (clouds, fog, godrays) that uses delta tracking and ratio tracking on density fields instead of sphere tracing on distance, allowing for heterogeneous (non-uniform) density distributions [S1].

The claim states that Heterogeneous Volumetric Raymarching is a rendering technique for participating media (clouds, fog, godrays) that uses delta tracking and ratio tracking on density fields instead of sphere tracing on distance, allowing for heterogeneous (non-uniform) density distributions. *   **RHI Limitations:** The engine's RHI lacks 3D texture support (no depth field in `TextureDesc`, no samplers, bilinear interpolation is hand-written) [S1].

The claim states that the engine's RHI lacks 3D texture support, specifically noting 'no depth field in TextureDesc', 'no samplers', and 'bilinear interpolation is hand-written'. Source [S1] explicitly confirms these details in the passage: 'the RHI has no 3D textures. src/rhi/Resources.h:21-27 is TextureDesc { width, height, format, usage, debug_name } — no depth field, no TextureType enum, and no 3D texture anywhere in the codebase. It also has no samplers at all — every texture is read by integer index and bilinear is hand-written'. All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
